items.stem: What should drive table design in Apache Cassandra?

options.text: The queries the application must answer
options.rationale: Correct: Cassandra is query-first, so tables are shaped around read access patterns.
Normalization and joins are a relational approach, not Cassandra's model.

options.text: Minimising total stored bytes above all else
options.rationale: Denormalization and duplication are expected to serve queries efficiently.
Row ordering comes from clustering columns, not insertion order of design.

items.explanation: Correct: Cassandra is query-first, so tables are shaped around read access patterns.

items.stem: Which statements about a Cassandra primary key are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: The partition key determines which node stores the row
options.rationale: Correct: the partition key is hashed to a token that maps to nodes.

options.text: Clustering columns control the sort order of rows within a partition
options.rationale: Correct: they define on-disk ordering inside each partition.

options.text: The primary key enforces foreign-key relationships
options.rationale: Cassandra has no foreign keys or referential integrity.

options.text: Any column can be used in WHERE without being part of the key or an index
options.rationale: Filtering generally requires key columns or an explicit index.

items.explanation: Correct: the partition key is hashed to a token that maps to nodes.; Correct: they define on-disk ordering inside each partition.

items.stem: With replication factor 3, why do QUORUM writes and QUORUM reads return consistent data?

options.text: A write to 2 replicas and a read from 2 replicas are guaranteed to overlap on at least one node
options.rationale: Correct: when read replicas + write replicas exceed RF, their sets must intersect.

options.text: QUORUM writes to all 3 replicas synchronously
options.rationale: QUORUM requires a majority (2 of 3), not all replicas.

options.text: Cassandra locks the partition during the write
options.rationale: Cassandra does not use locking for this; it relies on replica overlap.

options.text: Reads always go to a single master replica
options.rationale: There is no master; QUORUM contacts a majority of replicas.

items.explanation: Correct: when read replicas + write replicas exceed RF, their sets must intersect.
